samples.text:
The table shows the sales of four products of a company in each quarter of 2024 in thousands of units.

Overall, the sales of most products increased during the year and the fourth quarter was the best, with 640 thousand units in total. Product D sold the most in the year, 770 thousand.

Product D sold 200 thousand in Q1, but then the sales decreased to 190 and 160 thousand in Q2 and Q3. After that it went up again to 220 thousand in Q4. Product A increased every quarter, it started at 120 thousand and reached 210 thousand in Q4, and the total was 615 thousand.

Product C was the lowest in Q1 with only 45 thousand, but it grow very fast to 60, 95 and then 140 thousand, so the year total were 340 thousand. On the other hand, Product B was the only product which sales fell. It sold 80 thousand at first and then 78, 75 and 70 thousand in the last quarter. It total was 303 thousand, the lowest.

The total sales went up from 445 thousand in Q1 to 463, 480 and 640 thousand.
samples.why: Overview present and figures accurate · every product covered but with too much mechanical detail and a trailing final paragraph · limited vocabulary · several verb-form and pronoun errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The table illustrates the number of units of four products (in thousands) that a company sold in each quarter of 2024 and the annual totals.

Overall, total sales increased throughout the year, with a particularly sharp rise in the final quarter. Product D was the best-selling item over the year, while Product C showed the fastest growth and Product B was the only one to decline.

The company's total sales grew gradually from 445 thousand units in Q1 to 480 thousand in Q3, before jumping to 640 thousand in Q4. Product D sold 200 thousand units in the first quarter but saw a decrease to 160 thousand in Q3. However, it recovered strongly to 220 thousand in Q4, reaching a yearly total of 770 thousand. Product A followed a steadier upward trend, rising from 120 to 210 thousand units, and its annual sales amounted to 615 thousand.

The most dramatic change was in Product C, whose sales more than tripled from 45 to 140 thousand over the year. As a result, its total of 340 thousand was higher than that of Product B, which fell slightly in each quarter from 80 to 70 thousand and achieved the lowest total of 303 thousand.
samples.why: Clear overview of the main trends and contrasts · key features well selected and logically sequenced · good range of cohesive devices · some less common collocations · frequent error-free sentences, slightly repetitive structure.

samples.text:
The table sets out quarterly sales figures, in thousands of units, for four products sold by a company in 2024, together with their totals for the year.

Overall, the company's combined sales rose in every quarter, surging in the last three months of the year. Product D was the top seller over the year, but the most striking trend was the rapid expansion of Product C, in contrast to the gradual decline of Product B.

Combined sales edged up from 445 thousand in Q1 to 480 thousand in Q3, before leaping by a third to 640 thousand in Q4. Product D accounted for the largest share of annual sales, at 770 thousand units, although its performance was uneven: sales slipped from 200 to 160 thousand between Q1 and Q3 before rebounding to 220 thousand. Product A, meanwhile, grew in each quarter, from 120 to 210 thousand, for a total of 615 thousand.

Product C began the year as the weakest performer, at just 45 thousand, yet its sales rose more than threefold to 140 thousand by Q4, lifting its annual total to 340 thousand. Product B, by contrast, recorded a steady fall from 80 to 70 thousand, leaving it with the lowest total of 303 thousand.
samples.why: Well-placed overview contrasting growth and decline · data selected judiciously with accurate proportional change · cohesion managed skilfully · wide, precise trend vocabulary · varied complex structures, error-free.
